sections.title: Series solutions of linear second-order ODEs
Singular points and the method of Frobenius

variables.meaning: the coefficients a₀, a₁, a₂, … of a power series Σ a_k(x − x₀)^k, written a_k
the coefficients b_k of a second power series added to or multiplied with the first
the terms c_k of a series Σ c_k in the ratio and root tests, and the coefficients c_k = a₀b_k + a₁b_{k−1} + ⋯ + a_kb₀ of the product of two power series
the partial sum S_n(x) = Σ_{k=0}^n a_k(x − x₀)^k of a power series, its terms up to the nth power
the radius of convergence of a power series, ρ = ∞ allowed: the series converges absolutely on (x₀ − ρ, x₀ + ρ) and diverges outside it
an analytic function f(x), one equal to its Taylor series for x near a given point x₀
the kth derivative f^{(k)}(x₀) of f(x) at the point x₀, the kth Taylor coefficient's numerator
the dependent variable, an unknown function
the derivative of y, the same as dy/dx
the dependent variable, an unknown function
the derivative of y, the same as dy/dx
the second derivative of y
the coefficients a_k of the power series solution y = Σ a_k(x − x₀)^k, determined by the recurrence relation from the arbitrary a₀ and a₁
the first of the two series solutions of a second-order equation, with y₁(0) = 1 and y₁′(0) = 0, the series in a₀
the second of the two series solutions of a second-order equation, with y₂(0) = 0 and y₂′(0) = 1, the series in a₁, so that y = a₀y₁ + a₁y₂
the dependent variable, an unknown function
the derivative of y, the same as dy/dx
the second derivative of y
the coefficients a_k of a Frobenius-type solution y = Σ a_k x^{k+r}, found from the recurrence once r is known
the coefficients b_k of the second solution y₂ = Σ b_k x^{k+r} + (ln x) y₁
the exponent r of a Frobenius-type solution y = x^r Σ a_k x^k, a real number, not necessarily an integer, a root of the indicial equation
the larger root of the indicial equation, the exponent of the first Frobenius-type solution
the second root of the indicial equation, the exponent of the second solution
the first Frobenius-type solution, from the first (or only) root of the indicial equation
the second linearly independent solution, a Frobenius-type solution from the second root or a series with a logarithm term
an analytic function f(x), a power series, the factor in the ansatz y = x^r f(x)
the Bessel function of the first kind J_p(x) of order p, a constant multiple of y₁ that solves Bessel's equation of order p; J_{−p} the one of order −p
the Bessel function of the second kind Y_n(x) of integer order n, the limit of (cos(pπ)J_p − J_{−p})/sin(pπ) as p → n, linearly independent of J_n
the gamma function Γ(x) = ∫₀^∞ t^{x−1}e^{−t} dt, with Γ(x + 1) = xΓ(x) and Γ(n) = (n − 1)! for positive integers n
